You may get a much more smooth service from Blizzard, you may enjoy the old content, but like modern retail, your interest dwindles when nothing more happens. That's truly why Nostalrius thrived. That's why MoltenWoW thrived, That's why ScapeGaming thrived. It was more community based, social, and fun in nature.

It'd be great if the servers would require you to have an active wow account - that way blizzard would know that the more legacy servers there are - the more money they have.

And it's only fair too - otherwise people who just don't want to pay the monthly fee will be playing on the legacy servers, making it an actual "pirate" server.

I'd even go so far as to propose the opposite of what you proposed with the "license" idea: Have blizzard pay the legacy servers a small % of each player's monthly fee per player using that server (as long as they make sure all the players have active accounts). Basically allow them to monetize making people have fun.

That would be a great way to give back to the community while strengthening their brand and their (paying) userbase. It's literally a win-win-win situation.

Blizzard could never actively pay private servers. That would cut into their profits dramatically. It's super easy to setup a private WoW server. I've already made one myself. There's no way blizzard could actively monitor all of the thousands of active or to-be active private servers. That's why I think the servers should legally run by paying a license fee. It could be X amount a month or it could scale with server size and the amount of money it takes to manage the server. hosting, development, etc.

Having Blizzard in full monetary control of private servers would be the doom of legacy in a whole. No server would be able to prosper when Blizzard forces them to do something that that individual community doesn't agree with.

Because that's the case, I don't personally think Blizzard should be at the helm of running legacy servers, rather, I believe they should open up the ability to license servers. That way the private servers that are still running, and there are hundreds of them, can continue to run and grow, while making Blizzard some money. Nostalrius could come back under a new name and everyone could be happy.

On top of that they would have legit scripting and be more accurate to the original experiences. Nostalrius did a great job, but lets not kid ourselves here it was not a 100% blizz-like experience. Private servers are judged by how blizz-like they are and Nostalrius was one of the--if not the--best out there.

Just based on Blizzard saying that they don't even have the old code base anymore, I'd assume they'd have to emulate it just like the private servers do. That is, if they are to be believed. That would also lead to a non-blizz-like experience unless it's given actual dev time, which costs money.

They said that? I personally find that hard to believe (that they don't have the original code anymore, not that they said that). It seems odd that instead of archiving old source files for such a massive and popular game that they would just discard them forever.

I'm looking for the panel they had a while back that they specifically said, "even if we wanted to do it, we couldn't because the code base is gone for it." -- Paraphrased I'm pretty sure, but they went on to say that rather than build new bases for each expansion they just incrementally updated code which is why legacy isn't possible, because it no longer exists.

While the people who want legacy servers have my full sympathy (and I still think taking down Nostalrius was a painfully bad decision on the side of Blizzard), I still hold that people would eventually get bored of them due to the lack of new content (with Nostalrius already planning to switch from Classic to BC, if I remember correctly).

Another thing that irks me is my personal belief that most people mainly hope to find the same type of experience in legacy servers they had in Classic WoW. But this simply won't be the case - even if the game mechanics may be the same as back in the day, the sense of mystery which WoW had before Wiki sites and item databases popped up like mushrooms is irrevocably lost. Likewise, player behavior has also changed over the years - for many, WoW was their first MMORPG, but after oh-so-many-years, these formerly new players for which Classic was a new and exciting experience have learned how MMORPGs work, and are unlikely to receive the same experience simply by replaying old content - both for themselves, and for other players.

TL/DR: Legacy servers essentially live by virtue of the thick glasses which nostalgia googles have. But no matter how thick the glass, a pure legacy server will not keep people entertained for more than a few months at its best, not to speak of the fact that you technically need at least three servers or else people will complain - PvE, PVP, and RP.

So let people get bored of them. Blizzard could be turning a profit on those people until they do get bored. What you and Blizzard aren't getting here is that this is a major missed opportunity for them to make money to do practically nothing. Let the private servers collect a fee - split that fee with blizzard. If it ever stops being profitable they can pull the plug. Everyone wins.
